page: The Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is an instance within the High Frequency Compute family, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled on a shared allocation model. Operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, and FMA instructions. The server includes 32 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a bundled 512 GB NVMe solid-state drive and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero dedicated GPUs provided.

Benchmark evaluations highlight notable strengths in data compression and memory access tests. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 41.55 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, complemented by strong results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.91 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing. The PassMark memory test also ranked in the top tier at 3,043.43. Overall compute throughput settled squarely in the median ranges, recording a PassMark CPU score of 16,168.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,016.0. In contrast, large-block uncached memory operations and 7B parameter LLM inference exhibited reduced throughput.

Given its combination of balanced compute resources, 512 GB NVMe storage, and dependable compression and memory benchmarks, the vhf-8c-32gb provides an economical configuration for general-purpose server workloads. It is functionally well suited for web serving, continuous integration builds, Redis caching, microservices, and medium-scale database hosting.

The system includes 32 GB of system memory, 16 MB of L3 cache, a bundled 512 GB NVMe SSD, and one allocated public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution in single-threaded gzip compression and PassMark memory operations, alongside strong text processing and bzip3 decompression performance. Overall multi-core CPU metrics and Redis transactions remain in the median tier, whereas uncached large-block memory bandwidth and 7B LLM inference show limitations. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory distribution and high-speed local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for general web serving, application backends, CI/CD runners, and transactional database tasks.
